Definition: from G193; want of self-restraint:--excess, incontinency.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and both times of a lack of self-control. Jesus tells the Pharisees their cups are clean outside but within they are full of extortion and excess; and Paul tells married couples not to deprive one another except it be with consent for a time, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency. The word is the absence of restraint — appetite with no master.
TheologicalSignificance: The word is a warning about what happens when nothing says no. I believe both uses point the same way: excess is not freedom, it is slavery to appetite, and the cure is the self-control the Spirit gives, not the willpower we wish we had.
